title: Systems Thinking in Project Quality Management
subject: Project quality management
description: Twenty-five questions across easy, medium and hard on how systems thinking explains project quality, its principles, tools and benefits over traditional thinking.

questions.prompt: What is systems thinking in project quality management?
options: A method of inspecting each activity separately
An approach that views a project as an interconnected system whose activities, resources, processes and stakeholders influence one another
A statistical technique for sampling deliverables
A checklist of quality standards for suppliers
questions.explanation: Systems thinking treats the project as one connected whole, so quality is not managed in isolation.

questions.prompt: In simple terms, what does systems thinking mean?
options: Focusing on the most expensive activity first
Managing each department independently
Looking at the entire project as one integrated system rather than at individual activities separately
Dealing with problems only when they occur
questions.explanation: All project components must work together for the final outcome to meet the required standards.

questions.prompt: What does systems thinking mainly focus on understanding?
options: The cost of each isolated activity
The ranking of defects by frequency
The order in which audits are carried out
The relationships, interactions and interdependencies among the parts of a system
questions.explanation: The notes describe it as a management philosophy built on understanding how parts of a system relate to one another.

questions.prompt: Which principle says that all project activities are connected, so a problem in one can affect others?
options: Interdependence
Holistic perspective
Feedback mechanism
Dynamic behaviour
questions.explanation: The example is poor-quality cement affecting structural strength, safety and the overall quality of the building.

questions.prompt: Which principle means looking at the entire project rather than at individual departments or activities?
options: Feedback mechanism
Holistic perspective
Dynamic behaviour
Continuous improvement
questions.explanation: A project manager using this principle considers design, procurement, construction, inspection and customer satisfaction together.

questions.prompt: What is a feedback mechanism in this context?
options: Reporting project costs to the client each month
A plan for sharing profits among suppliers
Replacing workers after defects are found
Collecting information about project performance and using it to improve processes
questions.explanation: Customer complaints and inspection reports are the lecture's examples of feedback.

questions.prompt: Which tool shows how different project activities are connected?
options: Process mapping
FMEA
Root cause analysis
Fishbone diagram
questions.explanation: Process mapping shows connections between activities. FMEA identifies potential failures, root cause analysis finds underlying causes, and the fishbone diagram identifies possible causes of problems.

questions.prompt: Which ISO 9001 principle encourages managing interrelated processes as a coherent system?
options: Customer focus
Leadership
Process approach
Relationship management
questions.explanation: The notes state that the process approach is the principle closest to the systems view.

questions.prompt: Which example illustrates the interdependence principle?
options: Reducing the procurement budget, leading to inferior materials and higher maintenance costs
Customer complaints guiding corrective actions
A company regularly reviewing its construction procedures to reduce defects
Poor-quality cement affecting structural strength, safety and the overall quality of a building
questions.explanation: The procurement budget example belongs to interrelationships, the complaints example to feedback, and the procedure review to continuous improvement.

questions.prompt: What does the interrelationships principle recognise?
options: All activities are connected in exactly the same way
Changes in one part of a project may produce consequences in another part
Projects stay constant over time
Quality is determined by a single department
questions.explanation: Reducing the procurement budget may lead to inferior materials and later to higher maintenance costs.

questions.prompt: Under the holistic perspective, what should a project manager consider when evaluating project quality?
options: Design, procurement, construction, inspection and customer satisfaction
Construction and inspection only
Procurement cost and schedule only
The performance of the quality department alone
questions.explanation: The holistic perspective looks at the whole project instead of individual departments.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a feedback mechanism in the notes?
options: Regular salary reviews for project staff
Competitive tendering to select contractors
Customer complaints and inspection reports used to identify quality problems and introduce corrective actions
Reducing the budget for materials
questions.explanation: Feedback means using performance information to improve processes.

questions.prompt: A construction company regularly reviews its procedures to reduce defects and improve productivity. Which principle is this?
options: Continuous improvement
Interdependence
Dynamic behaviour
Holistic perspective
questions.explanation: Systems thinking encourages continuous evaluation and improvement of project processes.

questions.prompt: According to the dynamic behaviour principle, why must project quality management adapt over time?
options: Because quality standards are rewritten every month
Because resources, technology, risks, stakeholder expectations and environmental conditions change
Because projects repeat the same cycle of defects
Because suppliers are always replaced
questions.explanation: Projects change over time, so quality management has to adapt to those changes.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of project stage and application of systems thinking is correct?
options: Project design: monitor performance and identify defects
Project closure: coordinate people, materials, technology and processes
Procurement: select suppliers based on quality requirements
Project initiation: integrate quality standards into project plans
questions.explanation: Initiation identifies quality expectations and stakeholder requirements, planning integrates standards into plans, design considers safety, cost, performance and reliability, execution coordinates people, materials, technology and processes, and quality control monitors performance.

questions.prompt: What does the systems dynamics tool examine?
options: The sequence of project activities
Potential failures, their causes and their consequences
How performance information influences future decisions
How changes in one project variable influence other variables over time
questions.explanation: The last option describes feedback loops, and the second describes FMEA.

questions.prompt: Which tool identifies potential failures, their causes and their consequences?
options: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA)
Feedback loops
Process mapping
Systems dynamics
questions.explanation: FMEA looks ahead at what could fail and what that would cause.

questions.prompt: In the road project, the design is excellent but inferior materials are used. What does the systems-thinking interpretation say?
options: The road will be sound, because design determines overall quality
The road may fail prematurely, because quality results from the combined performance of all components
Only the materials supplier is responsible, so other components need no review
The road will last, because inspection will correct the materials
questions.explanation: Likewise, high-quality materials may not give a durable road if workers use incorrect procedures.

questions.prompt: Which pairing of road component and quality contribution is correct?
options: Supervision: ensures durable construction materials
Equipment: ensures competent project execution
Maintenance planning: supports long-term road performance
Inspection: ensures appropriate engineering specifications
questions.explanation: Design ensures appropriate specifications, materials ensure durability, labour ensures competent execution, equipment ensures accurate and efficient construction, supervision ensures compliance, and inspection identifies defects.

questions.prompt: Which pairing correctly contrasts traditional thinking with systems thinking?
options: Traditional: examines interconnected problems; systems: treats problems separately
Traditional: considers long-term consequences; systems: focuses on short-term results
Traditional: encourages integrated decisions; systems: encourages isolated decisions
Traditional: often addresses symptoms; systems: investigates underlying causes
questions.explanation: Traditional thinking also focuses on individual activities and departments, while systems thinking focuses on the entire project and overall performance.

questions.prompt: A manager measures only each department's own performance and makes isolated decisions. Which style is this, and what is the systems alternative?
options: Traditional thinking; systems thinking emphasises overall project performance and integrated decisions
Systems thinking; traditional thinking emphasises overall performance
Traditional thinking; systems thinking focuses on short-term results
Systems thinking; it needs no integration between departments
questions.explanation: Emphasising departmental performance and isolated decisions is typical of traditional thinking.

questions.prompt: Which is a listed challenge of applying systems thinking?
options: Too few interdependencies between activities
Difficulty in identifying relationships between project variables
An excess of reliable project information
Projects that never change
questions.explanation: The listed challenges also include complexity of project activities, poor communication, resistance to change, inadequate management commitment, lack of reliable information and limited skills.

questions.prompt: What is the key academic takeaway of the notes?
options: Project quality is determined mainly by the quality department
Project quality depends chiefly on the materials used
Project quality is the result of final inspection
Project quality is a system-wide outcome resulting from the integration and interaction of people, processes, materials, technology, resources and management decisions
questions.explanation: Quality does not come from one department, individual or activity.

questions.prompt: A team collects inspection reports and customer complaints but never uses them to change how work is done. Which principle is missing?
options: Interdependence
Holistic perspective
Feedback mechanism
Dynamic behaviour
questions.explanation: Feedback only helps when performance information is used to improve processes.

questions.prompt: Which set lists the ISO 9001 principles that systems thinking is closely associated with?
options: Planning, assurance, control, audit, closure and handover
Prevention, appraisal, internal failure, external failure and conformance
Scope, time, cost, quality, risk and procurement
Process approach, leadership, improvement, evidence-based decision-making, relationship management and customer focus
questions.explanation: The process approach is the closest match, because it manages interrelated processes as a coherent system.
